title: PRAY THIS BEFORE YOU EAT BREAKFAST AND EVERY SPIRITUAL CHAIN WILL BREAK
text: Before you touch that spoon, before you pour that tea, before your lips taste anything this morning, I need you to understand what is actually happening in the spirit realm in the first 60 minutes after your eyes open. There is a window, narrow, sacred, easily wasted, and what you do inside that window determines whether you walk into your day as a free man or as a man still dragging something. He doesn't even realize he's attached to his ankle. I am not asking you to skip breakfast. I am asking you to understand what breakfast represents and why the order of your morning matters more than you have ever been told. Something in me stirred this morning because I know there is somebody reading this who has been eating their way past their deliverance for years, not out of rebellion, but out of ignorance. Nobody ever told you that the enemy is patient enough to wait for your first bite because he knows that once your body is satisfied, your spirit stops reaching. Let the fire fall on every dull spirit right now before another word is spoken. Shakala my red dawn, fire of the early hour, awaken every sleeping spirit before the body is satisfied. I want to take you to something in the life of the man Job, a man who understood the weight of divine priority in a way many of us have never grasped. Job 23:12 says, "Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food." Read that again. More than my necessary food. Job is not saying he despised food. He's saying that when it came to ranking priorities, the voice of God outranked even the food his body legitimately needed to survive. This is not extremism. This is order. This is a man who understood that the soul has a hunger the stomach cannot satisfy, and if you feed the stomach before you feed the soul, you will walk around all day physically full and spiritually starving. This is the revelation behind everything we are about to do together. Before you eat breakfast, there is a spiritual transaction that wants to happen. And if you rush past it for the sake of convenience, you are not committing a sin, but you are missing an appointment. And some of the chains that have held your life hostage for years are not going to break through a Sunday service or a conference altar call. They are going to break in the quiet, unglamorous space of your kitchen before your first bite, when nobody is watching and nobody is clapping. I decree this morning, every chain that has been waiting for you to simply show up in that window of priority is about to snap. Fire of priority fall now. Re catch baram tole. Fire of first things. Re align every misplaced priority in this house this morning. There is something else I want you to see because it would change how you view your mornings permanently. Mark chapter 1 verse 35 tells us that Jesus, rising up a great while before day, departed into a solitary place and there prayed. I want you to notice this was not an occasional discipline for Jesus. This was pattern. The Son of God who had every legal right to walk in unbroken authority without lifting a finger in prayer still chose to rise before the sun, before the demands of the day, before the crowds, before food, and positioned himself in communion with the Father. If the sinless Son of God needed that window, what makes any of us think we can skip it and still walk in the same authority he walked in? This morning, I am not simply teaching you a habit. I am inviting you into a pattern that the master himself modeled, and patterns carry power that isolated events do not. Let's talk about chains because I don't want this to remain abstract. When I say spiritual chains, I'm talking about anything that has kept you bound in a cycle you cannot seem to break through sheer human effort cycles of anger. You don't understand the root of cycles of financial setback that repeats no matter how hard you work, cycles of relationships that all seem to fail in the same pattern, cycles of sickness that keep returning after temporary relief, cycles of addiction, cycles of self-sabotage right at the point of breakthrough. Acts chapter 16 tells the story of Paul and Silas beaten, in prison, feet fastened in stocks, and at midnight they prayed and sang praises unto God, and suddenly there was a great earthquake so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone's bonds were loosed. I want you to notice the word everyone's, not just Paul and Silas. Every prisoner in that facility experienced the loosing because there is something about worship and prayer offered at an inconvenient hour, in an uncomfortable position, before relief comes, before comfort comes, before breakfast comes, that shakes foundations far beyond your own individual situation. When you pray before you eat this morning, you are not only loosing your own chains, you may be shaking foundations that affect people you don't even know are watching your life. Let earthquake fire fall on every prison holding somebody captive right now. Raj yesod baram, fire of the midnight shaking, loose every band and open every door before this day begins. I feel the anointing rising as I say this. There is a woman reading this whose situation has felt like Hannah's. 1 Samuel chapter 1 tells us Hannah was in bitterness of soul and prayed unto the Lord and wept sore before she ever went to eat. In fact, the scripture makes a specific point of telling us that after she poured out her heart before the Lord, she went her way and did eat and her countenance was no more sad. Notice the sequence again. Prayer first, then food, then transformation of countenance. Something happened in that order that would not have happened if she had eaten first and prayed as an afterthought. I decree over every woman carrying a Hannah level ache this morning. Barrenness of any kind, whether in the womb, in a dream, in a business, in a ministry, your countenance is about to change before this day is finished because you are choosing the order that God honors. Say this with your whole chest. I will not let my stomach lead my spirit. I will not let convenience outrank consecration. This morning before I eat, I position myself for breakthrough. Let Hannah grace fall on every aching heart. Shanana baruk, fire of transformed countenance, turn every heaviness into lightness before this day advances. I want to teach you something about the number of days you've allowed to pass without this kind of positioning because I sense the enemy has been counting on your business. Every single morning that you have rushed straight from your bed to your responsibilities without acknowledging the Lord first has been, in a sense, a morning where you signed a silent permission slip allowing the noise of the day to set the tone instead of the voice of heaven. Psalm 5:3 says, "My voice shall thou hear in the morning, O Lord. In the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee and will look up." That word direct in the original carries the sense of arranging in order like laying wood on an altar before lighting it, like a soldier arranging weapons before battle. David was not casually mentioning God in passing each morning. He was deliberately, strategically arranging his first thoughts, his first words, his first posture around the Lord before anything else had the chance to claim that space. This morning, I want you to reclaim every morning you have surrendered to noise. I want you to reclaim every chain-permitting morning where breakfast or your phone or your rush to work took the seats that belong to the Lord. Father, we repent this morning for every day we let convenience outrank consecration. We repent for treating prayer as an afterthought, squeezed into leftover minutes instead of the firstfruits of our day. Forgive us and restore to us what those mornings cost us. Let restoration fire fall on every stolen morning. Shuba Ghana, fire of restored mornings. Return everything that misplaced priority has cost this life. I sense something shifting now, and I want to bring in a picture from the book of Exodus that will help you understand exactly what kind of authority you are stepping into this morning. Before the children of Israel could leave Egypt, before the final plague broke their chains permanently, they had to do something specific with a lamb. They had to apply its blood to the door posts, and only after the blood was applied were they instructed on how to eat. >> [music] >> Exodus 12 tells us clearly that the order mattered. The blood first, applied in obedience, and then the meal, eaten with your loins girded, staff in hand, ready to move. This was not a random sequence. The blood had to go up before the food could go down, because the blood was what separated a house marked for judgement from a house marked for passage. This morning before you eat, I want you to consciously apply the blood of Jesus over your household, over your body, over your mind, over your finances, the same way Israel applied blood over their doorpost. Not because the blood needs reapplying, it was applied once perfectly at Calvary, but because you need the conscious act of remembering and declaring it over your specific situation this specific morning. Say this out loud, I apply the blood of Jesus over my body, my mind, my home, my finances, and my destiny this morning. Let every plague of delay, sickness, and confusion pass over this house. Let the blood speak. Dam Yeshua Kadosh, blood of the everlasting covenant, speak louder than every accusation raised against this life today. Now, I want to move into a season of declaration before we go deeper into prayer, because I feel the fire building and it needs an outlet. Say this boldly one after another, and let each one land before moving to the next. Before I eat breakfast this morning, every generational chain assigned to my bloodline is broken. Before I eat breakfast this morning, every chain of delay attached to my finances is severed. Before I eat breakfast this morning, every chain of sickness that has outlived its welcome in my body is snapped. Before I eat breakfast this morning, every chain of confusion clouding my next decision is shattered. Before I eat breakfast this morning, every chain of fear that has kept me small is broken off my mind. Before I eat breakfast this morning, every chain of shame from my past loses its grip on my present. Before I eat breakfast this morning, every chain holding my marriage, my family, my children in cycles of dysfunction is loosed. Before I eat breakfast this morning, I declare that I am walking into this day lighter than I have walked in years. Let every chain-breaking word take immediate effect. Shabakash mind fire of the immediate break, let every chain named this morning fall the sun reaches noon. I want to pause the fire for a moment and speak tenderly because I know somebody reading this is thinking I've prayed before, I've fasted before, and the chain is still there. I don't want to dismiss that pain. >> [music] >> Sometimes chains are stubborn not because God's power is insufficient, but because there has been an open door somewhere that keeps re-inviting the same bondage back in even after it's been broken. This is why before we go further into declarations, I want us to deal with doors, not just chains. 2 Corinthians 2:11 wants us to be alert lest Satan should get an advantage of us for we are not ignorant of his devices. One of his primary devices is re-entry through unaddressed doors, unforgiveness that was never released, agreements made in moments of despair, words spoken over your own life in anger, involvement with things that open access points you didn't fully understand at the time. This morning, before your chain-breaking prayer can hold long term, I want to lead you through closing doors, not just breaking chains. Because a broken chain with an open door is simply an invitation for a new chain to be forged. Father, we ask you to search us this morning. The way David asked in Psalm 139:23 and 24, search me, oh God, and know my heart. Try me and know my thoughts. And see if there be any wicked way in me and lead me in the way everlasting. Reveal every door we have unknowingly left open. Give us courage to close what needs closing, even if it costs us comfort, association, or habit. Let revelation fire fall and expose every hidden door. Pertach Mistagala, fire of exposure, reveal every hidden entry point before this day begins. I sense we are ready now to move into the deep prayer flow, the place where teaching gives way to travail, where declaration gives way to contending. I want you to settle into this next portion. Don't rush it. Don't scheme it. Let each line find its mark. Father, in the mighty name of Jesus, before we touch food this morning, we come first to touch you. We echo the cry of Psalm 63 verse 1. Oh God, thou art my God. Early will I seek thee. My soul thirsted for thee. My flesh longed for thee in a dry and thirsty land where no water is. Before the noise of today drowns out this quiet hour, we position ourselves here hungry for you more than we are hungry for anything on our table. We pray for destiny restoration this morning. For every assignment that has felt stuck, for every dream that has been dormant so long, it started to feel like a fantasy rather than a promise, we ask that the chain of delay be broken specifically over destiny. Let what was ordained before the foundation of the world begin to move visibly, tangibly, undeniably starting from this very day. We pray for family deliverance. Father, we bring before you every household where patterns keep repeating, patterns of absent fathers, patterns of overburdened mothers, patterns of siblings estranged over old wounds. We ask that the chain connecting one generation's pain to the next generation's repetition be severed this morning. Let this be the generation that breaks the cycle rather than extending it. We pray for marriage breakthrough. For every marriage where communication has broken down into silence or shouting, where intimacy has been replaced by roommate-like distance, we ask for the chains of misunderstanding to be broken. For hearts to soften toward one another again, and for covenant love to be rekindled with a strength greater than what first brought two people together. We pray for financial gates to open. Father, we renounce every chain of lack that has convinced hardworking hands that they will never see increase. According to Deuteronomy 28:12, you promised to open on to us your good treasure, the heaven, to give the rain on to our land in its season, and to bless all the work of our hand. We ask that every closed gate assigned to hold back rightful increase be broken open this morning before the sun climbs any higher. We pray for health and healing. We speak to every chronic condition that has become so familiar it started to feel permanent. Father, nothing is permanent that you have not authorized. We ask for chains of sickness to snap off bodies represented in this prayer. >> [music] >> For pain that has lingered too long to finally lift, and for strength to return to places that have felt weak for longer than anyone around you even realizes. We pray against every evil covenant, curse, and altar operating against our lives. Father, according to Galatians 3:13, Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us. We stand on that redemption this morning and renounce every altar, ancestral, personal, or unknowingly agreed to that has legal ground to speak curses over our mornings, our meals, our households, or our futures. We dissolve every such covenant by the blood of Jesus. Let dissolving fire fall on every illegitimate covenant. Farabitan fire of dissolution, break every covenant not authored by the hand of God. We pray for angelic intervention over the hours ahead of us today. Psalm 103:20 says, "Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word." Father, release angels assigned to strength, angels assigned to protection, and angels assigned to open doors we have never even thought to pray about, to move on our behalf in this exact window before we eat and throughout every hour after. We pray against witchcraft assigned to disrupt today and every day that follows this pattern of morning consecration. We bind every manipulative spirit working through jealousy, through gossip, through hidden agendas dressed as concern. We cancel every arrow fired in the secret place against our peace, our progress, and our provision. Let thunder scatter every hidden gathering against this life. Ra'am shiyol baram, thunder of judgment, scatter every gathering convened against this household. We pray for the restoration of time and virtue stolen through years of unconsecrated mornings, through seasons when the enemy successfully trained us to rush past our appointment with God for the sake of urgency that was never actually as urgent as it felt. We ask for that lost time, that drained virtue, to be restored and multiplied back to us. We pray for divine preservation over this day and every day going forward that we choose to walk in this pattern. Preserve our minds from destruction, our bodies from harm, our relationships from strive, and our spirits from complacency once the initial fire of this encounter begins to settle into ordinary life. Let preservation fire seal this entire prayer. Not such at amolam, fire of eternal preservation, seal every request prayed this morning as settled and secured. I want to bring in one more picture before we move into prophetic utterance because I believe it will anchor everything we've prayed. In Genesis chapter 32, Jacob wrestled with a man until the breaking of the day and refused to let go until he received a blessing. And scripture tells us that as he passed over Penuel, the sun rose upon him. I want you to notice Jacob did not eat before that wrestling. He did not rush the process for the sake of comfort. He stayed in the uncomfortable, exhausting place of contention until something shifted. And only after the sun rose upon him, marking the completion of his encounter, did life move forward with a new name. A new identity, a new authority. This morning, some of you have been trying to rush your deliverance the way you rush your coffee, quick, convenient, on the way to something else. I am asking you to consider what it would mean to wrestle a little longer, to stay a little past your comfort, to let the sun rise on you the way it rose on Jacob, marked by transformation rather than mere routine. Let Jacob grace fall on every wrestling spirit. Peniel or Zarephath, fire of the rising sun, mark this encounter as the place where limping became blessing. I feel a shift now toward prophetic utterance, spontaneous words I sense flowing from the spirit as we near the close of this encounter. There is somebody who has been waking up anxious for months, and the anxiety has felt like it arrives before you even fully wake. I hear the spirit saying, "That assignment ends this morning." What you do in this next hour is severing its access permanently. There is somebody whose appetite has changed recently, either eating too much to numb something or too little because grief has stolen your hunger. I hear the spirit saying, "I see what's underneath the eating pattern, and healing for the root is beginning today, not just management of the symptom." There is somebody who has tried this kind of morning prayer before and gave up after a few days because nothing seemed to change. I hear the spirit saying the seed was not wasted. It was building underground, and this time the breakthrough will be visible. There is somebody who has a family gathering coming up that you are dreading because of old tension. I hear the spirit saying, "Go in peace, not in armor." The grace to be different in that room has already been deposited in you this morning. There is somebody whose business has been leaking resources in ways you can't quite trace. I hear the spirit saying, "There is a hole that has been spiritually opened, and it is being sealed even as this word is spoken." The chain around that habit is looser than you think, but you have to actually pull. There is somebody who lost someone recently, and breakfast has felt strange, heavy, wrong. Somehow, I hear the spirit saying, "Grief is not a chain I'm asking you to break. It is a season I'm asking you to walk through with me. And I am closer in this than you realize. There is somebody whose children have wandered from what they were raised to believe, and every morning feels like a fresh wave of worry about them. I hear the spirit saying, "The prayers you've prayed have not evaporated. They are stored, and the appointed time of return is closer than the silence suggests. Let every word spoken settle into the exact life it was meant for." Dabana farmakon, fire of precise landing, let every prophetic word released this morning find its assigned address. As we begin to draw this to a close, I want to bring you back to the practical weight of what we've walked through, because revelation without application simply becomes another inspiring memory instead of a lifestyle. Isaiah 61:1 declares that the spirit of the Lord God is upon him, because the Lord has anointed him to preach good tidings onto the meek, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound. That liberty was proclaimed once at Calvary, finished and complete, but liberty proclaimed still requires a captive to walk out of the cell. Nobody drags you out. The door stands open, and you have to choose to walk through it morning after morning until walking through it becomes who you are, rather than something you occasionally remember to do. I am asking you this morning to make a decision, not just to feel something. Decide that tomorrow and the day after and the day after that this pattern continues not as a legalistic ritual but as a love language between you and the father a way of saying before anything else gets my attention today you get it first. Say this final decree with everything left in you from this morning forward I choose the order of heaven over the order of convenience. I choose consecration before consumption. I choose the voice of God before the noise of the day and because I choose this order every chain assigned to interrupt my destiny has already lost its legal ground to remain. Let final fire fall and seal this covenant of order. Shatam said the alarm fire of the eternal order seal this covenant of priority as an unbreakable pattern over this life. Go now and let your breakfast taste different this morning not because the food has changed but because you have. Walk out of this encounter lighter than you walked in freer than you have felt in longer than you can remember and carry this pattern forward until it is no longer a discipline you perform but a freedom you simply live in. It is broken it is loosed it is settled. Now go and eat in peace.
